narrative:
The model estimates a 55% chance that you will leave your current job. Because of this, the organization has decided to deny your promotion, as they are concerned about investing in someone who may not stay long-term.

The prediction is driven primarily by three key aspects of your profile. Most influential was the fact that you have attended 7 or more training programs in the last three years. This strongly pushed the model toward predicting you will stay, because employees who complete this many programs are generally more committed. However, two other factors outweighed this positive signal. Your overall career experience of 6–10 years pulled the prediction toward leaving, as people with this moderate level of total experience are more likely to explore new opportunities than those with either very little or a great deal of experience. Similarly, having spent 6–10 years in your current organization also contributed to the “will leave” direction, since most employees predicted to stay have either much shorter or much longer tenure here.

Taken together, these elements created a slight majority probability that you will depart. The organization should discuss your career goals with you openly. You may want to reflect on whether your satisfaction with recognition, workload balance, and job stability could be improved to reduce the risk of leaving. Addressing these openly could change the outlook for both sides. (218 words)
